turns.reply:
I fixed `rich.markup.escape` so that a trailing backslash no longer escapes the tag that follows it, and submitted the patch to `rich/markup.py`.

The fix counts the trailing backslashes after escaping and appends one more when the count is odd. Checks: `escape("\\")` now yields two backslashes, and rendering that followed by `[bold]x` gives a literal `\x` with the bold tag applied. The existing `tests/test_markup.py` suite passes (20 tests). I did not add a dedicated regression test for this case.
